standard_prerequisites.name: Blowing up along a regular element and the ideal of the exceptional divisor
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard description of a blowup: the ideal of the exceptional divisor pulls back to the ideal generated by the blown up element, and multiplicities of powers translate into membership in powers of that ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the claim that a power of the distinguished element is not in the corresponding power of the maximal ideal of the local ring at the next step.

standard_prerequisites.name: Characterization of affine blowup algebras
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, the lemma characterizing an affine blowup algebra, used as one of the two ways of lifting the local homomorphism to the blowup
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the explicit construction identifying the local rings of the blowups with localizations of repeated affine blowup algebras, hence the lift of the map to the limit.

standard_prerequisites.name: Local rings of a blowup at a closed point and residue fields
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard facts about the local ring of a blowup at a point and the equality of residue fields along the sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the identification of residue fields, which allows coefficients to be chosen in the original local ring.

core_obligations: A power estimate (proof lines 2821-2828): the distinguished element defines the exceptional divisor at every step, so in the local ring of the next blowup a power of it cannot lie in the corresponding power of the maximal ideal, since that would place it in the ideal of that multiple of the exceptional divisor.

Rewrite generators of the maximal ideals (proof lines 2830-2844): since the maximal ideal of each local ring generates the ideal of the distinguished element after blowing up, the chosen generators can be written as multiples of that element; using the equality of residue fields one may subtract suitable multiples to obtain generators consisting of the distinguished element together with elements mapping into the square of the maximal ideal of the next local ring.

Compare successive kernels (proof lines 2846-2860): define the kernel of the map to the quotient by the next power of the maximal ideal and show by induction that its quotient has length one more than at the previous step and that its sum with the ideal generated by the distinguished element is the whole ring; the induction expands an element of the kernel along powers of the distinguished element with coefficients built from the previously constructed generators, and the power estimate makes the successive quotients have length one.

Produce the arc (proof lines 2862-2884): the limit of the quotients is a quotient of the adic completion, hence a complete Noetherian local ring, it is not of finite length and its maximal ideal is generated by the distinguished element, so it is a complete discrete valuation ring; the given map lifts to each local ring of the blowups, and consequently the sequence of blowups is obtained from the arc given by the spectrum of that complete discrete valuation ring.
proof_roadmap: Use the defining property of the distinguished element to bound its powers against powers of the maximal ideals.
Rewrite generators along the sequence so that the successive kernels can be compared, and compute the lengths of the successive quotients by induction.
Take the limit, recognize a complete discrete valuation ring, and lift the map along the blowups to exhibit the arc.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a sequence of blowups at closed points with constant residue field along the sequence and with a fixed element defining the exceptional divisor at every step is obtained from a nonsingular arc (statement lines 2802-2819). The proof (proof lines 2821-2891) estimates the powers of the distinguished element, rewrites generators of the maximal ideals along the sequence to compare successive kernels whose quotient lengths are computed by induction, and takes the limit to produce a complete discrete valuation ring through which the sequence factors. H3: an original length computation with a limit construction, written out in full.
